key_insight: LLIFT generates semi-synthetic brain MRI with realistic, spatially controlled lesions using only image-level labels or box masks, enabling ground-truth benchmarks for XAI evaluation.
clinical_relevance: This could help researchers test explainability methods on medical images where lesion location is known, without relying on imperfect manual pixel annotations.
method: LLIFT-GAN learns pathological features from binary class labels alone.
LLIFT-DM uses diffusion-based inpainting conditioned on bounding-box masks via ControlNet.
Both aim to place realistic lesions in user-controlled regions of healthy MRI scans.
evidence_signal: On Human Connectome Project brain MRI data, both variants achieved Fréchet Inception Distance scores comparable to the real healthy-vs-pathological gap, and qualitative review found lesion structures realistic.
watch_item: The generated images are for benchmark creation rather than direct clinical use, and realism or generalization may depend on the source dataset and chosen lesion region.
paper_title: Local Label-Informed Feature Transfer for Generating Ground-Truth Medical Images: A Comparison of GAN- and Diffusion-Based Approaches
